title: Der Krautesel
source: Brüder Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmärchen, Band 2, 7. Auflage (Ausgabe letzter Hand), Dieterich, Göttingen 1857, KHM 122. Text from Wikisource („Der Krautesel (1857)“, twice proofread against the original). Fresh translation made directly from the German; 1857 spelling preserved exactly.
about: KHM 122 (Der Krautesel) gives a huntsman a wishing-cloak and a swallowed bird's heart that leaves a gold piece under his pillow each morning, both gifts from a beggar-woman he was kind to — and both are taken from him in turn by a witch's beautiful daughter, who drugs him into surrendering the bird's heart and later strands him on a mountain of gems after making off with the cloak. Carried off by a passing cloud instead of the giants who find and spare him there, he lands in a walled garden and learns by hard experience that one kind of cabbage growing there turns a man into a donkey and another turns him back; disguised, he carries a head of each to the witch's castle and feeds the bad kind to the witch, her maid and, after a moment's hesitation, his faithless beloved as well, driving all three off to a miller to be worked and fed according to how much each deserves. The witch dies of the treatment, but the huntsman relents toward the other two, restores the girl once she confesses she acted under her mother's threats, and — unusually for this corner of the collection — the tale ends in a marriage that actually sounds happy. Spelling follows the 1857 edition, so you will meet older forms such as daß, gieng, ward, Noth and Reichthum.

sentences.t: Es war einmal ein junger Jäger, der gieng in den Wald auf Anstand.
sentences.l: There was once a young huntsman, that one went into the forest on the watch for game.
sentences.i: Once there was a young huntsman, and he went into the forest to lie in wait for game.
sentences.n: Es war einmal is the fixed opening of a German tale, our “once upon a time.” auf Anstand gehen is the hunter’s phrase: to take up a stand and wait for the game to come. der gieng carries on with a demonstrative, “that one went,” where English uses a relative. gieng is the 1857 spelling of ging.

sentences.t: Er hatte ein frisches und fröhliches Herz, und als er daher gieng und auf dem Blatt pfiff,
sentences.l: He had a fresh and cheerful heart, and as he went along and piped on the leaf,
sentences.i: He had a fresh and merry heart, and as he went along piping on a leaf,
sentences.n: auf dem Blatt pfeifen: to whistle on a leaf held between the lips — countryman’s music, and also a hunter’s way of calling game. daher gehen is to come or go along.

sentences.t: kam ein altes häßliches Mütterchen, das redete ihn an und sprach „guten Tag, lieber Jäger, du bist wohl lustig und vergnügt,
sentences.l: there came an old ugly little mother, it addressed him and said “good day, dear huntsman, you are merry and content enough,
sentences.i: there came an old ugly little woman; she addressed him and said, “Good day, dear huntsman, you are merry and content enough,
sentences.n: Mütterchen, the diminutive of Mutter, is a kindly word for an old woman; being a diminutive it is neuter, so the tale says das and es. anreden: to address, speak to — separable. wohl here is “no doubt, well enough,” not “well.”

sentences.t: aber ich leide Hunger und Durst, gib mir doch ein Almosen.“
sentences.l: but I suffer hunger and thirst, do give me an alms.”
sentences.n: Hunger leiden: to suffer hunger, go hungry — no article, as German likes in such pairs. doch in a command is a nudge: “do give.”

sentences.t: Da dauerte den Jäger das arme Mütterchen, daß er in seine Tasche griff und ihr nach seinem Vermögen etwas reichte.
sentences.l: Then the poor little mother moved the huntsman to pity, so that he reached into his pocket and handed her something according to his means.
sentences.i: Then the huntsman was moved to pity for the poor old woman, so that he reached into his pocket and gave her what he could.
sentences.n: jemanden dauern is an impersonal verb turned the other way round from English: the person pitied is the subject and the pitier stands in the accusative — den Jäger dauerte das Mütterchen, “the little mother caused the huntsman pity.” nach seinem Vermögen: according to his means.

sentences.t: Nun wollte er weiter gehen, aber die alte Frau hielt ihn an, und sprach „höre, lieber Jäger, was ich dir sage, für dein gutes Herz will ich dir ein Geschenk machen:
sentences.l: Now he wanted to go further, but the old woman held him back, and said “hear, dear huntsman, what I tell you: for your good heart I will make you a present:
sentences.i: Now he was for going on, but the old woman stopped him and said, “Listen, dear huntsman, to what I tell you: for your good heart I will make you a gift:
sentences.n: anhalten: to stop, hold back — separable, with an at the end. höre is the singular imperative; she uses du to a young man, as an old woman may. ein Geschenk machen is the German for giving a present.

sentences.t: geh nur immer deiner Wege, über ein Weilchen wirst du an einen Baum kommen, darauf sitzen neun Vögel, die haben einen Mantel in den Krallen und raufen sich darum.
sentences.l: just keep going your ways, over a little while you will come to a tree, on it sit nine birds, they have a cloak in their claws and are scuffling over it.
sentences.i: just go your way, and in a little while you will come to a tree; nine birds are sitting on it, they have a cloak in their claws and are fighting over it.
sentences.n: deiner Wege gehen is an old genitive phrase, “to go one’s ways.” nur immer with an imperative means “just keep going.” darauf, “thereon,” points back to the tree; sich raufen um is to scuffle over something.

sentences.t: Da lege du deine Büchse an und schieß mitten drunter:
sentences.l: Then level you your gun and shoot right in among them:
sentences.i: Then take aim with your gun and shoot into the middle of them:
sentences.n: die Büchse anlegen: to level a gun, to take aim — separable, an at the end. du after the imperative lege is the older emphatic subject, “do you shoot.” drunter is darunter, “among them.”

sentences.t: den Mantel werden sie dir wohl fallen lassen, aber auch einer von den Vögeln wird getroffen sein und todt herab stürzen.
sentences.l: the cloak they will surely let fall for you, but one of the birds too will be hit and plunge down dead.
sentences.i: they will let the cloak fall for you, sure enough, but one of the birds will be hit as well and drop down dead.
sentences.n: dir is the dative of interest — they let it fall “for you.” fallen lassen: to let fall. todt is the 1857 spelling of tot, and the tale prints herab stürzen as two words where modern German joins them.

sentences.t: Den Mantel nimm mit dir, es ist ein Wunschmantel, wenn du ihn um die Schultern wirfst, brauchst du dich nur an einen Ort zu wünschen, und im Augenblick bist du dort.
sentences.l: The cloak take with you, it is a wishing-cloak, when you throw it about your shoulders you need only wish yourself to a place, and in a moment you are there.
sentences.i: Take the cloak with you; it is a wishing-cloak: when you throw it round your shoulders you need only wish yourself to a place, and in an instant you are there.
sentences.n: Den Mantel is put first for emphasis, which pushes the imperative nimm in behind it. sich wünschen is reflexive, “to wish oneself” somewhere; brauchen … nur zu is “need only.” Wunschmantel — wish-cloak — is the tale’s own compound.

sentences.t: Aus dem todten Vogel nimm das Herz heraus, und verschluck es ganz, dann wirst du allen und jeden Morgen früh beim Aufstehen ein Goldstück unter deinem Kopfkissen finden.“
sentences.l: Out of the dead bird take the heart out, and swallow it whole, then you will each and every morning early on getting up find a gold piece under your pillow.”
sentences.i: Take the heart out of the dead bird and swallow it whole, and then every morning when you rise you will find a gold piece under your pillow.”
sentences.n: herausnehmen keeps its particle heraus at the end although Aus dem todten Vogel already stands in front — German is willing to say the direction twice. allen und jeden Morgen is emphatic doubling, “each and every morning.” beim Aufstehen is an infinitive used as a noun, “at the getting-up.”

sentences.t: Der Jäger dankte der weisen Frau und dachte bei sich „schöne Dinge, die sie mir versprochen hat, wenns nur auch all so einträfe.“
sentences.l: The huntsman thanked the wise woman and thought to himself “fine things that she has promised me, if only they all came true so.”
sentences.i: The huntsman thanked the wise woman and thought to himself, “Fine things she has promised me — if only they all came true.”
sentences.n: danken takes the dative, der weisen Frau. bei sich denken: to think to oneself. einträfe is the subjunctive of the wish, with wenns nur, “if only”; all stands uninflected for alles. die weise Frau is the wise woman of the tales, half herb-doctor and half something else.

sentences.t: Doch, wie er etwa hundert Schritte gegangen war, hörte er über sich in den Ästen ein Geschrei und Gezwitscher, daß er aufschauete:
sentences.l: Yet, when he had gone about a hundred paces, he heard above him in the branches a screaming and twittering, so that he looked up:
sentences.i: But when he had gone some hundred paces, he heard above him in the branches such a screaming and twittering that he looked up:
sentences.n: daß here gives the result, “so that.” Ge- put before a verb makes a noun for the continuous noise of it: Geschrei, screaming; Gezwitscher, twittering. aufschauete is an older long past form, modern schaute auf.

sentences.t: da sah er einen Haufen Vögel, die rissen mit den Schnäbeln und Füßen ein Tuch herum, schrien, zerrten und balgten sich, als wollts ein jeder allein haben.
sentences.l: there he saw a heap of birds, they tore a cloth about with their beaks and feet, screamed, dragged and scuffled, as if each one wanted to have it alone.
sentences.i: and there he saw a crowd of birds tearing a cloth this way and that with their beaks and feet, screaming, dragging and scuffling, as if each wanted it for himself alone.
sentences.n: ein Haufen: a heap, a crowd. herumreißen: to tear this way and that. sich balgen: to tussle. als wollts is the subjunctive after als, “as if it wanted”; wollts is wollte es. What the old woman called a Mantel the tale here calls only a Tuch, a cloth — the huntsman does not yet know what he is looking at.

sentences.t: „Nun,“ sprach der Jäger, „das ist wunderlich, es kommt ja gerade so, wie das Mütterchen gesagt hat,“
sentences.l: “Now,” said the huntsman, “that is strange, it comes about just so as the little mother said,”
sentences.i: “Well,” said the huntsman, “this is strange: it is falling out exactly as the old woman said,”
sentences.n: wunderlich is “odd, strange.” ja gerade so: just exactly so. The speech closes with a comma inside the quotation mark, because the sentence runs straight on into what he did next.

sentences.t: nahm die Büchse von der Schulter, legte an und that seinen Schuß mitten hinein, daß die Federn herumflogen.
sentences.l: took the gun from the shoulder, levelled it and did his shot right into the middle, so that the feathers flew about.
sentences.i: and he took the gun from his shoulder, took aim, and fired his shot into the middle of them, so that the feathers flew about.
sentences.n: anlegen again, this time with no object: legte an, “took aim.” einen Schuß thun: to make a shot; that is the 1857 spelling of tat. daß once more means “so that.”

sentences.t: Alsbald nahm das Gethier mit großem Schreien die Flucht, aber einer fiel todt herab, und der Mantel sank ebenfalls herunter.
sentences.l: At once the creatures took flight with great screaming, but one fell down dead, and the cloak sank down likewise.
sentences.i: At once the creatures took to flight with a great screaming, but one fell down dead, and the cloak came sinking down as well.
sentences.n: die Flucht nehmen: to take flight. das Gethier (modern Getier) is a collective for beasts and takes a singular verb though it means them all. herab and herunter both say “down here,” toward the watcher.

sentences.t: Da that der Jäger wie ihm die Alte geheißen hatte, schnitt den Vogel auf, suchte das Herz, schluckte es hinunter und nahm den Mantel mit nach Haus.
sentences.l: Then the huntsman did as the old woman had bidden him, cut the bird open, sought the heart, swallowed it down and took the cloak with him home.
sentences.i: Then the huntsman did as the old woman had bidden him: he cut the bird open, sought out the heart, swallowed it down, and took the cloak home with him.
sentences.n: heißen with a dative and a plain clause is the old “to bid, to order”: wie ihm die Alte geheißen hatte. die Alte, “the old one,” is an adjective used as a noun. aufschneiden: to cut open, separable.

sentences.t: Am andern Morgen, als er aufwachte, fiel ihm die Verheißung ein, und er wollte sehen ob sie auch eingetroffen wäre.
sentences.l: On the other morning, when he awoke, the promise fell into his mind, and he wanted to see whether it had also come true.
sentences.i: The next morning, when he awoke, the promise came into his mind, and he wanted to see whether it had come true.
sentences.n: einfallen: to occur to someone — the thing remembered is the subject and the person stands in the dative, ihm. am andern Morgen: on the next morning. eintreffen is to come to pass, to be fulfilled; wäre is subjunctive after ob.

sentences.t: Wie er aber sein Kopfkissen in die Höhe hob, da schimmerte ihm das Goldstück entgegen und am andern Morgen fand er wieder eins, und so weiter jedesmal, wenn er aufstand.
sentences.l: But when he lifted his pillow up into the height, the gold piece shimmered toward him, and on the next morning he found one again, and so on every time when he got up.
sentences.i: But when he lifted his pillow up, the gold piece glinted at him, and the next morning he found another, and so on every time he rose.
sentences.n: in die Höhe heben: to lift up, “into the height.” entgegenschimmern: to shine toward someone, the person once more in the dative — ihm. und so weiter is “and so on.”

sentences.t: Er sammelte sich einen Haufen Gold, endlich aber dachte er „was hilft mir all mein Gold, wenn ich daheim bleibe?
sentences.l: He gathered himself a heap of gold, but at last he thought “what helps me all my gold, if I stay at home?
sentences.i: He gathered himself a heap of gold, but at last he thought, “What good is all my gold to me if I stay at home?
sentences.n: sich sammeln with a dative: to gather for oneself. helfen takes the dative, mir, so the German asks “what helps me?” where English asks “what good is it to me?”

sentences.t: ich will ausziehen und mich in der Welt umsehen.“
sentences.l: I will set out and look about me in the world.”
sentences.n: ausziehen: to set out, to leave home — separable, and one of the fixed motions of the tales. sich umsehen: to look about oneself.

sentences.t: Da nahm er von seinen Eltern Abschied, hieng seinen Jägerranzen und seine Flinte um und zog in die Welt.
sentences.l: Then he took leave of his parents, hung his huntsman’s knapsack and his musket about him and moved into the world.
sentences.i: Then he took leave of his parents, slung on his hunting-pack and his musket, and went out into the world.
sentences.n: Abschied nehmen von: to take leave of. umhängen: to hang about oneself, to sling on — separable, and the um comes only after both objects. hieng is the 1857 spelling of hing.

sentences.t: Es trug sich zu, daß er eines Tages durch einen dicken Wald kam, und wie der zu Ende war, lag in der Ebene vor ihm ein ansehnliches Schloß.
sentences.l: It carried itself to that one day he came through a thick forest, and when it was at an end, there lay in the plain before him a considerable castle.
sentences.i: It came to pass that one day he came through a thick forest, and when it ended there lay before him in the plain a fine castle.
sentences.n: sich zutragen: to come to pass, to happen — reflexive and separable, and the literal keeps its odd shape visible. eines Tages is the genitive of time, “one day.” ansehnlich is “considerable, imposing,” literally worth the looking at.

sentences.t: In einem Fenster desselben stand eine Alte mit einer wunderschönen Jungfrau und schaute herab.
sentences.l: In a window of the same stood an old woman with a wonderfully beautiful maiden and looked down.
sentences.i: At one of its windows stood an old woman with a wondrously beautiful maiden, looking down.
sentences.n: desselben, “of the same,” is the older way of saying “of it, its.” herab is “down hither”: the tale watches from below, standing where the huntsman stands.

sentences.t: Die Alte aber war eine Hexe und sprach zu dem Mädchen „dort kommt einer aus dem Wald, der hat einen wunderbaren Schatz im Leib, den müssen wir darum berücken, mein Herzenstöchterchen:
sentences.l: But the old woman was a witch and said to the girl “there comes one out of the forest, he has a wondrous treasure in his body, him we must ensnare for that reason, my heart’s little daughter:
sentences.i: But the old woman was a witch, and she said to the girl, “There comes a man out of the forest; he has a wondrous treasure in his body, and for that we must beguile him, my heart’s little daughter:
sentences.n: berücken is an old word for luring or ensnaring, as a bird is taken with lime. darum: for that reason. Herzenstöchterchen doubles the endearment — heart’s-little-daughter — and the caress is also an order; she is the witch’s own daughter.

sentences.t: uns steht das besser an als ihm.
sentences.l: that suits us better than him.
sentences.i: it becomes us better than it does him.
sentences.n: anstehen with a dative: to suit, to become someone. This one line is the witch’s whole justification, and the tale lets it stand without comment.

sentences.t: Er hat ein Vogelherz bei sich, deshalb liegt jeden Morgen ein Goldstück unter seinem Kopfkissen.“
sentences.l: He has a bird’s heart on him, that is why every morning a gold piece lies under his pillow.”
sentences.n: bei sich haben: to have on one, to carry. jeden Morgen is the accusative of time, marking a repeated occasion.

sentences.t: Sie erzählt ihr wie es damit beschaffen wäre und wie sie darum zu spielen hätte,
sentences.l: She tells her how it was constituted with it and how she was to play for it,
sentences.i: She told her how the matter stood and how she was to play for it,
sentences.n: The tale slips into the present tense, erzählt, in the middle of a past narrative — spoken storytelling does this, and the literal keeps it. wie es damit beschaffen ist: how matters stand with it. um etwas spielen: to play, to gamble for something. wäre and hätte are the subjunctive of reported speech.

sentences.t: und zuletzt drohte sie und sprach mit zornigen Augen „und wenn du mir nicht gehorchst, so bist du unglücklich.“
sentences.l: and at last she threatened and said with angry eyes “and if you do not obey me, then you are unhappy.”
sentences.i: and at last she threatened her and said with angry eyes, “And if you do not obey me, it will go badly with you.”
sentences.n: gehorchen takes the dative, mir. so after a wenn-clause is the answering “then.” unglücklich sein is weaker in the letter than in the intent — it is a threat, and the idiomatic line says what the words are meant to do rather than what they say.

sentences.t: Als nun der Jäger näher kam, erblickte er das Mädchen und sprach zu sich „ich bin nun so lang herumgezogen, ich will einmal ausruhen und in das schöne Schloß einkehren,
sentences.l: When now the huntsman came nearer, he caught sight of the girl and said to himself “I have now travelled about so long, I will rest for once and put up at the fine castle,
sentences.i: Now when the huntsman came nearer, he caught sight of the girl and said to himself, “I have been travelling about so long; I will rest for once and put up at the fine castle,
sentences.n: erblicken: to catch sight of. einkehren is the traveller’s word for turning in at a house for food and a night’s lodging. einmal, “for once,” softens the resolve.

sentences.t: Geld hab ich ja vollauf.“
sentences.l: money I have indeed in plenty.”
sentences.i: money I have in plenty enough.”
sentences.n: The object Geld stands first for emphasis. vollauf: in full measure. ja is the little word of emphasis, “after all, I certainly have.”

sentences.t: Eigentlich aber war die Ursache, daß er ein Auge auf das schöne Bild geworfen hatte.
sentences.l: But properly the cause was that he had cast an eye on the beautiful image.
sentences.i: But the real reason was that he had cast an eye on the lovely creature.
sentences.n: ein Auge auf etwas werfen: to cast an eye on something, just as in English. das Bild is “picture, image,” used here of the girl herself — she is a lovely thing to look at, and the tale words it so that she is not quite a person yet. eigentlich: properly speaking, really.

sentences.t: Er trat in das Haus ein, und ward freundlich empfangen und höflich bewirthet.
sentences.l: He stepped into the house, and was kindly received and courteously entertained.
sentences.n: eintreten: to step in, to enter — separable, so the ein comes at the end. ward is the old past of werden, here forming the passive. bewirthen (modern bewirten) is to entertain a guest with food and drink.

sentences.t: Es dauerte nicht lange, da war er so in das Hexenmädchen verliebt, daß er an nichts anders mehr dachte und nur nach ihren Augen sah, und was sie verlangte, das that er gerne.
sentences.l: It lasted not long, then he was so in love with the witch-girl that he thought of nothing else any more and looked only after her eyes, and what she desired, that he did gladly.
sentences.i: It was not long before he was so in love with the witch’s girl that he thought of nothing else, and had eyes for nothing but hers, and whatever she asked, that he did gladly.
sentences.n: verliebt in takes the accusative, in das Hexenmädchen. nach jemandes Augen sehen: to look toward someone’s eyes, to watch them for the least sign. was … das … is the correlative again, “whatever …, that ….”

sentences.t: Da sprach die Alte „nun müssen wir das Vogelherz haben, er wird nichts spüren, wenn es ihm fehlt.“
sentences.l: Then the old woman said “now we must have the bird’s heart, he will notice nothing when it is missing to him.”
sentences.i: Then the old woman said, “Now we must have the bird’s heart; he will notice nothing when it is gone.”
sentences.n: spüren: to feel, to notice. fehlen is “to be missing,” with the one who lacks in the dative — wenn es ihm fehlt, “when it is missing to him.”

sentences.t: Sie richteten einen Trank zu, und wie der gekocht war, that sie ihn in einen Becher und gab ihn dem Mädchen, das mußte ihn dem Jäger reichen.
sentences.l: They prepared a drink, and when it was cooked, she did it into a cup and gave it to the girl, that one had to hand it to the huntsman.
sentences.i: They prepared a draught, and when it had boiled, she put it into a cup and gave it to the girl, who had to hand it to the huntsman.
sentences.n: zurichten: to prepare, to make ready — separable, zu at the end. thun here is simply “to put.” das is the girl again, taken up as a demonstrative where English says “who.”

sentences.t: Sprach es „nun, mein Liebster, trink mir zu.“
sentences.l: Said it “now, my dearest, drink to me.”
sentences.i: She said, “Now, my dearest, drink to me.”
sentences.n: The verb comes first with no da before it — a lively narrative turn the tale uses often, “Said she.” zutrinken: to drink to someone, to pledge them; the zu stands at the end. es is the neuter Mädchen.

sentences.t: Da nahm er den Becher, und wie er den Trank geschluckt hatte, brach er das Herz des Vogels aus dem Leibe.
sentences.l: Then he took the cup, and when he had swallowed the draught, he broke the heart of the bird out of his body.
sentences.i: Then he took the cup, and when he had swallowed the draught, he brought the bird’s heart up out of his body.
sentences.n: brechen here is not “to break” but the old use for vomiting — the drink was an emetic; modern German would say erbrechen. des Vogels is the genitive, “of the bird.”

sentences.t: Das Mädchen mußte es heimlich fortschaffen und dann selbst verschlucken, denn die Alte wollte es haben.
sentences.l: The girl had to carry it off secretly and then swallow it herself, for the old woman wanted to have it.
sentences.n: fortschaffen: to carry away, to get rid of — separable. selbst: herself, in her own person. She does it under the threat of unit 29, which the tale does not repeat and has not forgotten.

sentences.t: Von nun an fand er kein Gold mehr unter seinem Kopfkissen, sondern es lag unter dem Kissen des Mädchens wo es die Alte jeden Morgen holte:
sentences.l: From now on he found no gold any more under his pillow, but it lay under the girl’s pillow where the old woman fetched it every morning:
sentences.i: From that time on he found no more gold under his pillow; it lay under the girl’s pillow, where the old woman fetched it every morning:
sentences.n: von nun an: from now on. kein … mehr is “no longer any.” In wo es die Alte holte, es is the gold as object and die Alte the subject — German marks who does what by case, not by order, so the words may stand in what looks to English like the wrong sequence.

sentences.t: aber er war so verliebt und vernarrt, daß er an nichts anders dachte, als sich mit dem Mädchen die Zeit zu vertreiben.
sentences.l: but he was so in love and besotted that he thought of nothing else than to drive the time away with the girl.
sentences.i: but he was so in love and so besotted that he thought of nothing but passing the time with the girl.
sentences.n: vernarrt, from Narr, a fool, is “made a fool of by love,” besotted. sich die Zeit vertreiben: to drive the time away, to pass the time. denken an takes the accusative.

sentences.t: Da sprach die alte Hexe „das Vogelherz haben wir, aber den Wunschmantel müssen wir ihm auch abnehmen.“
sentences.l: Then the old witch said “the bird’s heart we have, but the wishing-cloak we must take from him too.”
sentences.i: Then the old witch said, “The bird’s heart we have; but the wishing-cloak we must take from him as well.”
sentences.n: Both halves put the object first, which keeps the verb in second place: das Vogelherz haben wir. jemandem etwas abnehmen: to take something from someone, with the person in the dative.

sentences.t: Antwortete das Mädchen „den wollen wir ihm lassen, er hat ja doch seinen Reichthum verloren.“
sentences.l: Answered the girl “that one we will leave him, he has after all lost his riches.”
sentences.i: The girl answered, “Let us leave him that; he has lost his riches as it is.”
sentences.n: Verb-first narration again, Antwortete das Mädchen. den is the demonstrative standing for the cloak, “that one.” ja doch together are “after all, as it is.” Reichthum is the 1857 spelling of Reichtum. It is the one time the girl argues for him.

sentences.t: Da ward die Alte bös und sprach „so ein Mantel ist ein wunderbares Ding, das selten auf der Welt gefunden wird, den soll und muß ich haben.“
sentences.l: Then the old woman became angry and said “such a cloak is a wondrous thing that is seldom found in the world, that one I shall and must have.”
sentences.i: Then the old woman grew angry and said, “Such a cloak is a wondrous thing, seldom found in the world; have it I shall and must.”
sentences.n: ward is the old past of werden, “became”; bös werden is to grow angry. soll und muß piles two modals on the one infinitive haben — she will have it and there is an end of the matter.

sentences.t: Sie gab dem Mädchen Anschläge und sagte wenn es ihr nicht gehorchte, sollte es ihm schlimm ergehen.
sentences.l: She gave the girl instructions and said if it did not obey her, it should fare badly for it.
sentences.i: She gave the girl her instructions and said that if she did not obey her, it would go badly with her.
sentences.n: Anschläge are plans, designs, instructions for a stroke to be carried out. in sollte es ihm schlimm ergehen the es is the impersonal subject of ergehen — “it should go badly” — and ihm is the dative of the neuter Mädchen, so the badness lands on her. gehorchen takes the dative. The threat of unit 29 comes back in colder words.

sentences.t: Da that es nach dem Geheiß der Alten, stellte sich einmal ans Fenster und schaute in die weite Gegend, als wäre es ganz traurig.
sentences.l: Then it did according to the old woman’s bidding, placed itself once at the window and looked into the wide country, as if it were quite sad.
sentences.i: Then she did as the old woman bade her: she placed herself at the window and looked out into the wide country, as if she were very sad.
sentences.n: das Geheiß is the bidding, the command — a noun made from heißen. sich stellen: to place oneself. als wäre is the subjunctive of pretence, “as if she were,” and the point is that she is not.

sentences.t: Fragte der Jäger „was stehst du so traurig da?“
sentences.l: Asked the huntsman “what do you stand there so sadly?”
sentences.i: The huntsman asked, “Why do you stand there so sadly?”
sentences.n: Verb-first once more. was here is “why, what for,” an older use where modern German would say warum. dastehen: to stand there, separable.

sentences.t: „Ach, mein Schatz,“ gab es zur Antwort, „da gegenüber liegt der Granatenberg, wo die köstlichen Edelsteine wachsen.
sentences.l: “Ah, my treasure,” it gave for answer, “over there lies the garnet mountain, where the precious stones grow.
sentences.i: “Ah, my darling,” she answered, “over yonder lies the garnet mountain, where the precious stones grow.
sentences.n: zur Antwort geben: to give as answer. Schatz, “treasure,” is the everyday word for a sweetheart — and in this tale it is also literally what she is after. Granaten are garnets, the deep red stones; the tale has them growing like fruit.

sentences.t: Ich trage so groß Verlangen danach, daß wenn ich daran denke, ich ganz traurig bin;
sentences.l: I bear so great a longing for them that when I think of it, I am quite sad;
sentences.i: I have so great a longing for them that when I think of it I am quite cast down;
sentences.n: Verlangen tragen nach: to bear a longing for — a raised, old-fashioned phrase. groß stands uninflected before Verlangen, which older German allows. danach and daran both point back to the stones.

sentences.t: aber wer kann sie holen! nur die Vögel, die fliegen, kommen hin, ein Mensch nimmermehr.“
sentences.l: but who can fetch them! only the birds, which fly, come there, a human being nevermore.”
sentences.i: but who can fetch them! Only the birds, which fly, come there — a human being never.”
sentences.n: nimmermehr: never, nevermore. The last clause has no verb at all: ein Mensch nimmermehr, with kommt hin understood from what has just been said.

sentences.t: „Hast du weiter nichts zu klagen,“ sagte der Jäger, „den Kummer will ich dir bald vom Herzen nehmen.“
sentences.l: “Have you nothing further to complain of,” said the huntsman, “that grief I will soon take from your heart.”
sentences.i: “If that is all you have to complain of,” said the huntsman, “I will soon take that grief from your heart.”
sentences.n: A conditional without wenn: the verb comes first and the second half answers it. dir … vom Herzen is the dative of the person doing the work of an English possessive, “from your heart.” Kummer is grief, care.

sentences.t: Damit faßte er sie unter seinen Mantel und wünschte sich hinüber auf den Granatenberg, und im Augenblick saßen sie auch beide drauf.
sentences.l: With that he took her under his cloak and wished himself over onto the garnet mountain, and in a moment they were both sitting on it.
sentences.i: With that he took her under his cloak and wished himself across to the garnet mountain, and in an instant they were both sitting on it.
sentences.n: hinüber: over there, away from where one stands. sich wünschen with a place: to wish oneself somewhere. drauf is darauf, “on it.”

sentences.t: Da schimmerte das edele Gestein von allen Seiten daß es eine Freude war anzusehen, und sie lasen die schönsten und kostbarsten Stücke zusammen.
sentences.l: There the noble stone glittered from all sides so that it was a joy to look at, and they gathered the finest and costliest pieces together.
sentences.i: There the noble stones glittered on every side, so that it was a joy to behold, and they gathered up the finest and costliest pieces.
sentences.n: Gestein is a collective — all the stone of a place at once — so the German verb is singular where English wants a plural. edele is the older inflected form of edle. zusammenlesen: to gather up, to glean, with zusammen at the end.

sentences.t: Nun hatte es aber die Alte durch ihre Hexenkunst bewirkt, daß dem Jäger die Augen schwer wurden.
sentences.l: But now the old woman had brought it about through her witch’s art that to the huntsman the eyes grew heavy.
sentences.i: But the old woman had brought it about by her witchcraft that the huntsman’s eyes grew heavy.
sentences.n: bewirken: to bring about, to effect; the es looks forward to the daß-clause that explains it. dem Jäger is again the dative of the person where English uses a possessive, “the huntsman’s eyes.”

sentences.t: Er sprach zu dem Mädchen „wir wollen ein wenig niedersitzen und ruhen, ich bin so müde, daß ich mich nicht mehr auf den Füßen erhalten kann.“
sentences.l: He said to the girl “we will sit down a little and rest, I am so tired that I can hold myself no longer on my feet.”
sentences.i: He said to the girl, “Let us sit down a little and rest; I am so tired that I can no longer keep on my feet.”
sentences.n: wir wollen with an infinitive is the German “let us.” niedersitzen: to sit down, with nieder as its particle. sich erhalten: to keep, to maintain oneself.

sentences.t: Da setzten sie sich, und er legte sein Haupt in ihren Schooß und schlief ein.
sentences.l: Then they set themselves down, and he laid his head in her lap and fell asleep.
sentences.n: Haupt is the elevated word for a head — and it will come back in this tale meaning a head of lettuce, which is worth remembering when it does. Schooß is the 1857 spelling of Schoß, the lap. einschlafen: to fall asleep, separable.

sentences.t: Wie er entschlafen war, da band es ihm den Mantel von den Schultern und hieng ihn sich selbst um, las die Granaten und Steine auf und wünschte sich damit nach Haus.
sentences.l: When he had fallen asleep, it unbound the cloak from his shoulders and hung it about itself, gathered the garnets and stones up and wished itself with them home.
sentences.i: When he had fallen asleep, she loosed the cloak from his shoulders and hung it about herself, gathered up the garnets and stones, and wished herself home with them.
sentences.n: entschlafen is the raised word for falling asleep, and also the word used for dying, which gives the moment its shade. ihm … von den Schultern is the dative of the person, “from his shoulders.” sich umhängen: to hang about oneself; auflesen: to gather up. The betrayal is done in four plain verbs and not one word of comment.

sentences.t: Als aber der Jäger seinen Schlaf ausgethan hatte und aufwachte, sah er daß seine Liebste ihn betrogen und auf dem wilden Gebirg allein gelassen hatte.
sentences.l: But when the huntsman had done his sleep out and awoke, he saw that his dearest had cheated him and left him alone on the wild mountain.
sentences.i: But when the huntsman had slept his sleep out and awoke, he saw that his beloved had betrayed him and left him alone on the wild mountain.
sentences.n: seinen Schlaf austhun (modern austun) is “to do one’s sleep out,” to sleep one’s fill. betrügen: to cheat, to betray. Gebirg (modern Gebirge) is the high wild country, a whole range rather than one hill.

sentences.t: „O,“ sprach er, „wie ist die Untreue so groß auf der Welt!“
sentences.l: “Oh,” said he, “how is the faithlessness so great in the world!”
sentences.i: “Oh,” said he, “how great is faithlessness in the world!”
sentences.n: wie … so is an old exclamatory doubling that English cannot keep — “how so great.” die Untreue takes the article where English drops it.

sentences.t: saß da in Sorge und Herzeleid und wußte nicht was er anfangen sollte.
sentences.l: sat there in care and heart-sorrow and did not know what he should begin.
sentences.i: and he sat there in care and heartache and did not know what to do.
sentences.n: The subject is not repeated: the German runs straight on from the speech into saß. Herzeleid is heart-sorrow, grief. was anfangen: what to begin, what to do about it.

sentences.t: Der Berg aber gehörte wilden und ungeheuern Riesen, die darauf wohnten und ihr Wesen trieben, und er saß nicht lange, so sah er ihrer drei daher schreiten.
sentences.l: But the mountain belonged to wild and monstrous giants, who dwelt on it and drove their doings, and he sat not long, then he saw three of them come striding along.
sentences.i: But the mountain belonged to wild and monstrous giants, who lived on it and went about their business; and he had not sat long before he saw three of them come striding up.
sentences.n: gehören takes the dative, so the owners stand in that case. sein Wesen treiben: to carry on, to go about one’s doings. ihrer drei is the old partitive genitive, “three of them.” und … so joins the two clauses by parataxis where English wants “before.”

sentences.t: Da legte er sich nieder, als wäre er in tiefen Schlaf versunken.
sentences.l: Then he laid himself down, as if he had sunk into deep sleep.
sentences.i: Then he lay down as if he had sunk into a deep sleep.
sentences.n: sich niederlegen: to lay oneself down. als wäre … versunken is the subjunctive of pretence again — the same trick the girl played at the window.

sentences.t: Nun kamen die Riesen herbei, und der erste stieß ihn mit dem Fuß an und sprach „was liegt da für ein Erdwurm und beschaut sich inwendig?“
sentences.l: Now the giants came up, and the first knocked him with his foot and said “what sort of earth-worm is lying there and looking at itself inwardly?”
sentences.i: Now the giants came up, and the first pushed him with his foot and said, “What kind of earthworm is lying there looking at its own insides?”
sentences.n: anstoßen: to knock, to nudge — separable. was für ein is the fixed frame “what kind of,” in which für governs no case of its own. Erdwurm, “earth-worm,” is the giant’s word for a man. sich inwendig beschauen is genuinely obscure: it seems to mean the little creature is lost in contemplation of its own inside, but the phrase is rare and the sense is a guess.

sentences.t: Der zweite sprach „tritt ihn todt.“
sentences.l: The second said “tread him dead.”
sentences.i: The second said, “Trample him dead.”
sentences.n: todttreten: to tread to death, where the adjective todt supplies the result of the treading. tritt is the singular imperative of treten.

sentences.t: Der dritte aber sprach verächtlich „das wäre der Mühe werth!
sentences.l: But the third said contemptuously “that would be worth the trouble!
sentences.n: der Mühe werth: worth the trouble — werth (modern wert) governs the genitive. Said in the subjunctive, wäre, it means the flat opposite: it would not be worth the doing.

sentences.t: laßt ihn nur leben, hier kann er nicht bleiben, und wenn er höher steigt bis auf die Bergspitze, so packen ihn die Wolken und tragen ihn fort.“
sentences.l: let him only live, here he cannot stay, and if he climbs higher up to the mountain peak, then the clouds seize him and carry him off.”
sentences.i: just let him live; he cannot stay here, and if he climbs higher, up to the peak, the clouds will seize him and carry him off.”
sentences.n: laßt is the plural imperative to the other two. nur again is “just.” The present packen … tragen stands for the future, as German freely allows. die Wolken here are the ordinary clouds of the sky, and they act like living things — the tale offers no explanation and needs none.

sentences.t: Unter diesem Gespräch giengen sie vorüber, der Jäger aber hatte auf ihre Worte gemerkt, und sobald sie fort waren, stand er auf und klimmte den Berggipfel hinauf.
sentences.l: Under this talk they went past, but the huntsman had marked on their words, and as soon as they were gone, he stood up and climbed the mountain summit up.
sentences.i: Talking so, they passed by; but the huntsman had marked their words, and as soon as they were gone he rose and climbed up to the mountain summit.
sentences.n: unter here is “amid, in the course of,” not “under.” auf etwas merken: to pay heed to something. klimmen is the older strong verb for climbing, and hinauf, “up thither,” closes the clause.

sentences.t: Als er ein Weilchen da gesessen hatte, so schwebte eine Wolke heran, ergriff ihn, trug ihn fort und zog eine Zeitlang am Himmel her,
sentences.l: When he had sat there a little while, a cloud came floating up, seized him, carried him off and drew along the sky for a time,
sentences.n: heranschweben: to come floating up. eine Zeitlang is the accusative of duration, “for a time.” am Himmel her: along the sky, the her marking motion past the one who watches.

sentences.t: dann senkte sie sich und ließ sich über einen großen, rings mit Mauern umgebenen Krautgarten nieder,
sentences.l: then it sank itself and let itself down over a great cabbage-garden ringed about with walls,
sentences.i: then it sank and settled down over a great walled kitchen-garden,
sentences.n: sich senken and sich niederlassen are both reflexive: the cloud lowers itself, then lets itself down. rings mit Mauern umgeben is a participial phrase standing in front of its noun, which German does easily and English cannot follow. Krautgarten: a garden of Kraut — cabbages and greens.

sentences.t: also daß er zwischen Kohl und Gemüsen sanft auf den Boden kam.
sentences.l: so that he came gently to the ground between cabbage and garden greens.
sentences.n: also daß is “so that.” Kohl is cabbage and Gemüse the garden greens in general; the plural Gemüsen is older usage.

sentences.t: Da sah der Jäger sich um und sprach „wenn ich nur etwas zu essen hätte, ich bin so hungrig, und mit dem Weiterkommen wirds schwer fallen;
sentences.l: Then the huntsman looked about him and said “if only I had something to eat, I am so hungry, and with the getting-further it will fall hard;
sentences.i: Then the huntsman looked about him and said, “If only I had something to eat! I am so hungry, and it will go hard with me to get on from here;
sentences.n: sich umsehen: to look about oneself. hätte is the subjunctive of the wish, with nur, “if only.” das Weiterkommen is an infinitive used as a noun, “the getting further”; schwer fallen is “to come hard.” wirds is wird es.

sentences.t: aber hier seh ich keinen Apfel und keine Birne und keinerlei Obst, überall nichts als Krautwerk.“
sentences.l: but here I see no apple and no pear and no fruit of any kind, everywhere nothing but cabbage-stuff.”
sentences.i: but here I see no apple and no pear and no fruit of any kind — everywhere nothing but greenstuff.”
sentences.n: keinerlei: of no kind whatever. Obst is fruit in the ordinary High German sense. Krautwerk is a made collective — the whole business of Kraut, leaf and cabbage; the ending -werk gathers a mass of one thing.

sentences.t: Endlich dachte er „zur Noth kann ich von dem Salat essen, der schmeckt nicht sonderlich, wird mich aber erfrischen.“
sentences.l: At last he thought “at need I can eat of the salad, it does not taste particularly, but it will refresh me.”
sentences.i: At last he thought, “At a pinch I can eat some of the salad; it has no great taste, but it will refresh me.”
sentences.n: zur Noth: at need, at a pinch. von etwas essen: to eat “of” something, the partitive that English keeps in “eat some of.” sonderlich means “particularly,” and with a negative, “not much.”

sentences.t: Also suchte er sich ein schönes Haupt aus und aß davon, aber kaum hatte er ein paar Bissen hinab geschluckt, so war ihm so wunderlich zu Muthe, und er fühlte sich ganz verändert.
sentences.l: So he picked himself out a fine head and ate of it, but hardly had he swallowed a couple of bites down, then it was so strange to his mind, and he felt himself quite changed.
sentences.i: So he picked himself out a fine head and ate of it; but he had hardly swallowed a couple of mouthfuls when he felt very strange indeed, and quite altered.
sentences.n: ein Haupt is here a head of lettuce, not a person’s head — the same word that lay in the girl’s lap a few units back. sich aussuchen: to pick out for oneself, separable. mir ist zu Muthe (modern zumute) is the impersonal “I feel”: literally “it is so to my mind.” kaum … so is “hardly … when.”

sentences.t: Es wuchsen ihm vier Beine, ein dicker Kopf und zwei lange Ohren, und er sah mit Schrecken daß er in einen Esel verwandelt war.
sentences.l: There grew to him four legs, a thick head and two long ears, and he saw with horror that he had been changed into a donkey.
sentences.i: Four legs grew on him, a thick head and two long ears, and he saw with horror that he was turned into a donkey.
sentences.n: Es is a placeholder — “there grew” — with the real subject following the verb. ihm is the dative of the person the legs grow to. verwandeln in takes the accusative: changed into.

sentences.t: Doch weil er dabei immer noch großen Hunger spürte und ihm der saftige Salat nach seiner jetzigen Natur gut schmeckte, so aß er mit großer Gier immer zu.
sentences.l: Yet because he still felt great hunger at it and the juicy salad tasted good to him according to his present nature, he ate on with great greed.
sentences.i: Yet because he still felt a great hunger, and the juicy salad tasted good to him in his present nature, he went on eating with great greed.
sentences.n: schmecken works from the food’s side: the salad “tastes good to him,” with the eater in the dative. immer zu essen: to keep on eating. jetzig: present, of the moment. He is a donkey, and the tale reports his enjoyment of the salad without a word of pity.

sentences.t: Endlich gelangte er an eine andere Art Salat, aber kaum hatte er etwas davon verschluckt, so fühlte er aufs neue eine Veränderung, und kehrte in seine menschliche Gestalt zurück.
sentences.l: At last he got to another kind of salad, but hardly had he swallowed something of it, then he felt anew a change, and turned back into his human shape.
sentences.i: At last he came to another kind of salad, and hardly had he swallowed a little of it when he felt a fresh change and turned back into his human shape.
sentences.n: gelangen an: to reach, to come to. aufs neue: anew, afresh. zurückkehren: to turn back, to return, with zurück at the end.

sentences.t: Nun legte sich der Jäger nieder und schlief seine Müdigkeit aus.
sentences.l: Now the huntsman laid himself down and slept his weariness out.
sentences.i: Now the huntsman lay down and slept off his weariness.
sentences.n: ausschlafen: to sleep out, to sleep one’s fill — separable, and here it takes an object, seine Müdigkeit.

sentences.t: Als er am andern Morgen erwachte, brach er ein Haupt von dem bösen und eins von dem guten Salat ab und dachte „das soll mir zu dem Meinigen wieder helfen und die Treulosigkeit bestrafen.“
sentences.l: When he awoke on the next morning, he broke a head off the bad and one off the good salad and thought “that shall help me to my own again and punish the faithlessness.”
sentences.i: When he awoke the next morning, he broke off a head of the bad salad and one of the good, and thought, “This shall help me to my own again and punish their faithlessness.”
sentences.n: abbrechen: to break off — separable, and the ab comes only after both objects. das Meinige: what is mine, my own. Treulosigkeit is faithlessness, the breaking of troth; it is the tale’s own word for what was done to him.

sentences.t: Dann steckte er die Häupter zu sich, kletterte über die Mauer und gieng fort, das Schloß seiner Liebsten zu suchen.
sentences.l: Then he stuck the heads to himself, climbed over the wall and went off, the castle of his dearest to seek.
sentences.i: Then he stowed the heads about him, climbed over the wall, and went off to seek his beloved’s castle.
sentences.n: zu sich stecken: to put about one, into one’s own pockets. Häupter, the plural of Haupt, is heads of lettuce here. The infinitive with zu stands at the very end and carries the purpose.

sentences.t: Als er ein paar Tage herum gestrichen war, fand er es glücklicherweise wieder.
sentences.l: When he had roamed about a couple of days, he luckily found it again.
sentences.n: herumstreichen: to roam, to prowl about; it takes sein in the past, war … gestrichen, as verbs of motion do. The 1857 text prints herum gestrichen as two words.

sentences.t: Da bräunte er sich schnell sein Gesicht, daß ihn seine eigene Mutter nicht erkannt hätte, gieng in das Schloß und bat um eine Herberge.
sentences.l: Then he quickly browned himself his face, so that his own mother would not have recognised him, went into the castle and asked for a lodging.
sentences.i: Then he quickly stained his face brown, so that his own mother would not have known him, went into the castle, and asked for a night’s lodging.
sentences.n: sich das Gesicht bräunen: the sich is a dative of interest — he browns the face on himself. hätte … erkannt is the subjunctive of what would have been. um etwas bitten: to ask for something.

sentences.t: „Ich bin so müde,“ sprach er, „und kann nicht weiter.“
sentences.l: “I am so tired,” said he, “and cannot further.”
sentences.i: “I am so tired,” said he, “and can go no further.”
sentences.n: kann nicht weiter has no verb of motion in it: the modal kann with weiter carries “can go no further” by itself, and the literal leaves the gap where German leaves it.

sentences.t: Fragte die Hexe „Landsmann, wer seid ihr, und was ist euer Geschäft?“
sentences.l: Asked the witch “countryman, who are you, and what is your business?”
sentences.i: The witch asked, “Countryman, who are you, and what is your business?”
sentences.n: Landsmann is a fellow-countryman, used here as a friendly way of addressing a stranger. She says ihr, the respectful plural, to a man she does not know — and does not recognise. das Geschäft: business, errand.

sentences.t: Er antwortete „ich bin ein Bote des Königs und war ausgeschickt den köstlichsten Salat zu suchen, der unter der Sonne wächst.
sentences.l: He answered “I am a messenger of the king and was sent out to seek the most delicious salad that grows under the sun.
sentences.n: des Königs is the genitive, “of the king.” ausschicken: to send out. The superlative köstlichsten is the bait, and every word of his story is aimed at the old woman’s appetite.

sentences.t: Ich bin auch so glücklich gewesen ihn zu finden und trage ihn bei mir,
sentences.l: I have also been so fortunate as to find it and carry it with me,
sentences.i: I have been so fortunate as to find it, and I carry it with me,
sentences.n: so glücklich sein zu: to be so fortunate as to. bei mir tragen: to carry on one’s person.

sentences.t: aber die Sonnenhitze brennt gar zu stark, daß mir das zarte Kraut zu welken droht und ich nicht weiß ob ich es weiter bringen werde.“
sentences.l: but the sun’s heat burns far too strongly, so that the tender cabbage threatens to wilt on me and I do not know whether I shall bring it further.”
sentences.i: but the heat of the sun burns far too strong, so that the tender leaves threaten to wilt on me, and I do not know whether I shall get it any further.”
sentences.n: gar zu: far too. mir is the dative of the person concerned — it wilts “on me.” drohen with zu and an infinitive is “to threaten to.” Kraut here is the leaf of the salad itself.

sentences.t: Als die Alte von dem köstlichen Salat hörte, ward sie lüstern und sprach „lieber Landsmann, laßt mich doch den wunderbaren Salat versuchen.“
sentences.l: When the old woman heard of the delicious salad, she became greedy for it and said “dear countryman, do let me try the wondrous salad.”
sentences.i: When the old woman heard of the delicious salad, a craving came over her and she said, “Dear countryman, do let me taste the wondrous salad.”
sentences.n: lüstern werden: to be seized with craving. laßt is the respectful plural imperative, matching the ihr she has used all along. versuchen here is “to taste, to try” food.

sentences.t: „Warum nicht?“ antwortete er, „ich habe zwei Häupter mitgebracht und will euch eins geben,“ machte seinen Sack auf und reichte ihr das böse hin.
sentences.l: “Why not?” he answered, “I have brought two heads with me and will give you one,” made his sack open and handed her the bad one.
sentences.i: “Why not?” he answered. “I have brought two heads with me, and will give you one,” and he opened his sack and handed her the bad one.
sentences.n: aufmachen and hinreichen are both separable, and both particles fall at the ends of their clauses. das böse is the adjective standing alone for “the bad one.” The German runs the speech and the two actions on one subject.

sentences.t: Die Hexe dachte an nichts arges und der Mund wässerte ihr so sehr nach dem neuen Gericht, daß sie selbst in die Küche gieng und es zubereitete.
sentences.l: The witch thought of nothing wicked and the mouth watered her so much after the new dish that she went into the kitchen herself and prepared it.
sentences.i: The witch thought no harm, and her mouth watered so for the new dish that she went into the kitchen herself and prepared it.
sentences.n: das Gericht here is a dish of food, not a court of law — the one spelling serves both, and only the sentence tells you which. der Mund wässerte ihr: the mouth watered “to her,” the dative doing what English does with a possessive. nichts arges: nothing bad.

sentences.t: Als es fertig war, konnte sie nicht warten, bis es auf dem Tisch stand,
sentences.l: When it was ready, she could not wait until it stood on the table,
sentences.n: fertig: ready, finished. es is the dish. In German a dish stands on the table rather than sits on it.

sentences.t: sondern sie nahm gleich ein paar Blätter und steckte sie in den Mund,
sentences.l: but she took a couple of leaves at once and stuck them into her mouth,
sentences.n: sondern is the “but” that must follow a negative — nicht warten … sondern. gleich: at once, straight away.

sentences.t: kaum aber waren sie verschluckt, so war auch die menschliche Gestalt verloren, und sie lief als eine Eselin hinab in den Hof.
sentences.l: but hardly were they swallowed, then the human shape was lost too, and she ran as a she-donkey down into the yard.
sentences.i: but hardly were they swallowed when the human shape was lost as well, and she ran down into the yard as a she-donkey.
sentences.n: kaum … so: hardly … when. die Eselin is the female of Esel; German has a form for it and English has to say “she-donkey.” als here is “as, in the character of.”

sentences.t: Nun kam die Magd in die Küche, sah den fertigen Salat da stehen und wollte ihn auftragen,
sentences.l: Now the maid came into the kitchen, saw the finished salad stand there and wanted to carry it up,
sentences.i: Now the maid came into the kitchen, saw the salad standing there ready, and was about to serve it,
sentences.n: sah … stehen is the bare infinitive after a verb of perception, “saw it stand.” auftragen: to serve, to bring a dish to table.

sentences.t: unterwegs aber überfiel sie, nach alter Gewohnheit, die Lust zu versuchen, und sie aß ein paar Blätter.
sentences.l: but on the way there came over her, after old habit, the desire to taste, and she ate a couple of leaves.
sentences.i: but on the way, after her old habit, the longing to taste it came over her, and she ate a couple of leaves.
sentences.n: überfallen: to fall upon, to come over someone — the desire is the subject and sie the object. nach alter Gewohnheit: according to old habit; the tale lets us know she has done this before, and it costs her.

sentences.t: Alsbald zeigte sich die Wunderkraft, und sie ward ebenfalls zu einer Eselin und lief hinaus zu der Alten, und die Schüssel mit Salat fiel auf die Erde.
sentences.l: At once the miraculous power showed itself, and she became likewise a she-donkey and ran out to the old woman, and the bowl with salad fell on the ground.
sentences.i: At once the miraculous power showed itself: she too became a she-donkey and ran out to the old woman, and the bowl of salad fell to the ground.
sentences.n: zu etwas werden: to turn into something, with zu and the dative. sich zeigen: to show itself. ebenfalls: likewise, as well.

sentences.t: Der Bote saß in der Zeit bei dem schönen Mädchen, und als niemand mit dem Salat kam, und es doch auch lüstern danach war, sprach es „ich weiß nicht wo der Salat bleibt.“
sentences.l: The messenger sat in the time with the beautiful girl, and as nobody came with the salad, and it was greedy for it too, it said “I do not know where the salad is staying.”
sentences.i: The messenger sat meanwhile with the fair girl, and as nobody came with the salad, and she too was craving it, she said, “I do not know what is keeping the salad.”
sentences.n: in der Zeit: in that time, meanwhile. wo … bleibt is the German for “what is keeping” something — literally “where it is staying.” The tale calls him der Bote here, because a messenger is all she takes him for.

sentences.t: Da dachte der Jäger „das Kraut wird schon gewirkt haben“ und sprach „ich will nach der Küche gehen und mich erkundigen.“
sentences.l: Then the huntsman thought “the cabbage will surely have worked” and said “I will go to the kitchen and inquire.”
sentences.i: Then the huntsman thought, “The salad will have done its work by now,” and said, “I will go down to the kitchen and inquire.”
sentences.n: wird … gewirkt haben is the future perfect used for a confident guess: “will surely have worked by now,” with schon carrying that confidence rather than meaning “already.” sich erkundigen: to make inquiry.

sentences.t: Wie er hinab kam, sah er die zwei Eselinnen im Hof herum laufen, der Salat aber lag auf der Erde.
sentences.l: When he came down, he saw the two she-donkeys running about in the yard, but the salad lay on the ground.
sentences.n: sah … laufen, the bare infinitive after a verb of perception again. The 1857 text prints hinab kam and herum laufen as two words each where modern German joins them.

sentences.t: „Schon recht,“ sprach er, „die zwei haben ihr Theil weg“ und hob die übrigen Blätter auf, legte sie auf die Schüssel und brachte sie dem Mädchen.
sentences.l: “Quite right,” said he, “the two have their share away” and picked the remaining leaves up, laid them on the dish and brought them to the girl.
sentences.i: “All right,” said he, “those two have had their share,” and he gathered up the remaining leaves, laid them on the dish, and brought them to the girl.
sentences.n: schon recht is “all right, quite right,” said with satisfaction. sein Theil weg haben is a set phrase for having got one’s portion — and, said of a punishment, for having got what one deserved. Theil is the 1857 spelling of Teil.

sentences.t: „Ich bring euch selbst das köstliche Essen,“ sprach er, „damit ihr nicht länger zu warten braucht.“
sentences.l: “I bring you the delicious food myself,” said he, “so that you need not wait any longer.”
sentences.n: damit introduces the purpose, “so that.” nicht brauchen zu: not to need to. He keeps up the respectful ihr, still playing the king’s messenger to the last mouthful.

sentences.t: Da aß sie davon und war alsbald wie die übrigen ihrer menschlichen Gestalt beraubt und lief als eine Eselin in den Hof.
sentences.l: Then she ate of it and was at once, like the others, robbed of her human shape and ran as a she-donkey into the yard.
sentences.i: Then she ate of it and was at once robbed of her human shape like the others, and ran into the yard as a she-donkey.
sentences.n: berauben governs the genitive: ihrer menschlichen Gestalt beraubt, robbed “of her human shape.” Here the tale writes sie and ihrer, feminine, where it has been saying es of the same girl — the natural gender pushes through at the moment she loses her shape.

sentences.t: Nachdem sich der Jäger sein Angesicht gewaschen hatte, also daß ihn die Verwandelten erkennen konnten,
sentences.l: After the huntsman had washed himself his face, so that the transformed ones could recognise him,
sentences.n: nachdem is “after” as a conjunction. sich das Angesicht waschen — the dative sich again, washing the face on himself. das Angesicht is the elevated word for face. die Verwandelten: the transformed ones, an adjective used as a noun.

sentences.t: gieng er hinab in den Hof und sprach „jetzt sollt ihr den Lohn für eure Untreue empfangen.“
sentences.l: he went down into the yard and said “now you shall receive the wages for your faithlessness.”
sentences.n: The main clause follows the long nachdem-clause, so the verb gieng comes before its subject. der Lohn is wages, reward — used of a punishment it is grim. He says ihr to all three of them at once.

sentences.t: Er band sie alle drei an ein Seil und trieb sie fort, bis er zu einer Mühle kam.
sentences.l: He bound them all three to one rope and drove them off, until he came to a mill.
sentences.n: alle drei stands after the pronoun, as German prefers: sie alle drei. forttreiben: to drive away, separable.

sentences.t: Er klopfte an das Fenster, der Müller steckte den Kopf heraus und fragte was sein Begehren wäre.
sentences.l: He knocked at the window, the miller stuck his head out and asked what his desire was.
sentences.i: He knocked at the window; the miller put his head out and asked what he wanted.
sentences.n: an etwas klopfen: to knock at something. das Begehren is the desire, the request — a noun made from begehren. wäre is the subjunctive of the reported question.

sentences.t: „Ich habe drei böse Thiere,“ antwortete er, „die ich nicht länger behalten mag.
sentences.l: “I have three wicked beasts,” he answered, “which I no longer care to keep.
sentences.n: Thiere is the 1857 spelling of Tiere. mögen here is “to care to, to like to,” not “may.” böse: bad, wicked.

sentences.t: Wollt ihr sie bei euch nehmen, Futter und Lager geben, und sie halten wie ich euch sage, so zahl ich dafür was ihr verlangt.“
sentences.l: Will you take them in with you, give fodder and stall, and keep them as I tell you, then I pay for it what you ask.”
sentences.i: If you will take them in, give them fodder and a stall, and keep them as I tell you, then I will pay for it what you ask.”
sentences.n: Another conditional without wenn — the verb first, Wollt ihr, answered by so. das Lager is the beast’s bed, its litter. The present zahl stands for the future.

sentences.t: Sprach der Müller „warum das nicht? wie soll ich sie aber halten?“
sentences.l: Said the miller “why that not? but how am I to keep them?”
sentences.i: The miller said, “Why not? But how am I to keep them?”
sentences.n: warum das nicht: “why not that,” the das pointing back at the whole offer. soll is “am I to,” asking what is expected of him.

sentences.t: Da sagte der Jäger der alten Eselin, und das war die Hexe, sollte er täglich dreimal Schläge und einmal zu fressen geben;
sentences.l: Then the huntsman said, to the old she-donkey, and that was the witch, he should give daily three times blows and once to eat;
sentences.i: Then the huntsman said that to the old she-donkey — and that was the witch — he should give blows three times a day and food once;
sentences.n: der alten Eselin is dative, the one given to; the reported clause runs on with no daß to introduce it. fressen is the word used of an animal’s eating and never of a person’s, so zu fressen geben is “to give to feed.”

sentences.t: der jüngern, welche die Magd war, einmal Schläge und dreimal Futter;
sentences.l: to the younger, which was the maid, once blows and three times fodder;
sentences.n: The verb is not repeated: sollte er geben carries over from the last unit and English must supply it. welche is the older relative pronoun where modern German says die.

sentences.t: und der jüngsten, welche das Mädchen war, keinmal Schläge und dreimal zu fressen;
sentences.l: and to the youngest, which was the girl, no times blows and three times to eat;
sentences.i: and to the youngest, who was the girl, no blows at all and food three times;
sentences.n: keinmal is made on the pattern of einmal, dreimal — “no times, not once.” The three sentences are built as one scale, and the girl stands at the mild end of it.

sentences.t: denn er konnte es doch nicht über das Herz bringen, daß das Mädchen sollte geschlagen werden.
sentences.l: for he could after all not bring it over his heart that the girl should be beaten.
sentences.i: for he could not find it in his heart, after all, that the girl should be beaten.
sentences.n: es übers Herz bringen: to bring oneself to do something, literally “to bring it over one’s heart.” doch: after all, in spite of everything. The line gives away that he has forgiven her long before the tale says so.

sentences.t: Darauf gieng er zurück in das Schloß, und was er nöthig hatte, das fand er alles darin.
sentences.l: Thereupon he went back into the castle, and what he had need of, that he found all in it.
sentences.i: Thereupon he went back to the castle, and whatever he needed he found all of it there.
sentences.n: was … das … is the correlative once more. nöthig haben: to have need of (1857 spelling of nötig). darin: in it, within.

sentences.t: Nach ein paar Tagen kam der Müller und sprach er müßte melden daß die alte Eselin, die nur Schläge bekommen hätte und nur einmal zu fressen, gestorben wäre.
sentences.l: After a couple of days the miller came and said he had to report that the old she-donkey, which had got only blows and only once to eat, had died.
sentences.i: After a couple of days the miller came and said he must report that the old she-donkey, which had got nothing but blows and food only once, was dead.
sentences.n: müßte, hätte, wäre: three subjunctives in one sentence, all of them marking this as the miller’s report rather than the narrator’s statement. The relative clause is packed in between the subject and its verb, which German bears easily and English will not.

sentences.t: „Die zwei andern,“ sagte er weiter, „sind zwar nicht gestorben und kriegen auch dreimal zu fressen, aber sie sind so traurig, daß es nicht lange mit ihnen dauern kann.“
sentences.l: “The two others,” he said further, “have indeed not died and get their three feeds too, but they are so sad that it cannot last long with them.”
sentences.i: “The other two,” he went on, “have not died, and they get their three feeds as well, but they are so sad that it cannot last long with them.”
sentences.n: zwar … aber is the pair “to be sure … but.” es kann nicht lange mit ihnen dauern: it cannot go on long with them — that is, they are not far from death.

sentences.t: Da erbarmte sich der Jäger, ließ den Zorn fahren und sprach zum Müller er sollte sie wieder hertreiben.
sentences.l: Then the huntsman took pity, let the anger go and said to the miller he should drive them back here.
sentences.i: Then the huntsman took pity, let his anger go, and told the miller to drive them back.
sentences.n: sich erbarmen: to take pity — reflexive. den Zorn fahren lassen: to let one’s anger go, literally to let it drive off. hertreiben: to drive hither, toward the speaker.

sentences.t: Und wie sie kamen, gab er ihnen von dem guten Salat zu fressen, daß sie wieder zu Menschen wurden.
sentences.l: And when they came, he gave them of the good salad to eat, so that they became human beings again.
sentences.i: And when they came, he gave them some of the good salad to eat, so that they became human again.
sentences.n: von dem … zu fressen geben: to give some of a thing to eat, the von partitive. zu Menschen werden: to turn into people, zu again with the dative.

sentences.t: Da fiel das schöne Mädchen vor ihm auf die Knie und sprach „ach, mein Liebster, verzeiht mir was ich Böses an euch gethan, meine Mutter hatte mich dazu gezwungen;
sentences.l: Then the fair girl fell before him on her knees and said “ah, my dearest, forgive me what I have done evil to you, my mother had forced me to it;
sentences.i: Then the fair girl fell on her knees before him and said, “Ah, my dearest, forgive me the wrong I have done you; my mother had forced me to it;
sentences.n: verzeiht is the respectful plural imperative and euch keeps the same distance — she does not say du to him even now. verzeihen takes the dative of the person and the accusative of the thing forgiven. gethan is the 1857 spelling of getan, with the auxiliary habe left out as speech often leaves it. zwingen zu: to force to.

sentences.t: es ist gegen meinen Willen geschehen, denn ich habe euch von Herzen lieb.
sentences.l: it happened against my will, for I have you dear from the heart.
sentences.i: it was done against my will, for I love you with all my heart.
sentences.n: geschehen: to happen, to come to pass. jemanden lieb haben is the everyday German for loving someone, and von Herzen adds “from the heart.”

sentences.t: Euer Wunschmantel hängt in einem Schrank, und für das Vogelherz will ich einen Brechtrunk einnehmen.“
sentences.l: Your wishing-cloak hangs in a cupboard, and for the bird’s heart I will take an emetic draught.”
sentences.i: Your wishing-cloak hangs in a cupboard, and as for the bird’s heart, I will take a draught to bring it up.”
sentences.n: der Brechtrunk is a drink taken to make one vomit — the very means the witch used on him, now offered back. einnehmen is the verb for taking medicine.

sentences.t: Da ward er anderes Sinnes, und sprach „behalt es nur, es ist doch einerlei, denn ich will dich zu meiner treuen Ehegemahlin annehmen.“
sentences.l: Then he became of another mind, and said “just keep it, it is all one, for I will take you as my faithful wedded wife.”
sentences.i: Then he changed his mind and said, “Keep it; it is all one, for I will take you as my true wedded wife.”
sentences.n: anderes Sinnes werden is a genitive phrase, “to become of another mind.” einerlei: all one, no matter. Ehegemahlin is the raised word for a wedded wife. He answers her euch with du — the distance drops in the last line he speaks.

sentences.t: Und da ward Hochzeit gehalten, und sie lebten vergnügt mit einander bis an ihren Tod.
sentences.l: And then a wedding was held, and they lived contentedly with one another until their death.
sentences.i: And so the wedding was held, and they lived contentedly together to their death.
sentences.n: ward … gehalten is the passive formed with the old ward. Hochzeit halten takes no article. bis an ihren Tod: right up to their death — the closing formula of the tales.

glossary.aufstand: aufstehen — got up, rose (3rd sg. past; separable, prefix auf-)
glossary.ausziehen: ausziehen — to set out, leave home (separable, particle aus)
glossary.band: binden — bound, tied (3rd sg. past; band … von: untied from)
glossary.bring: bringen — bring (1st sg. present, short form of bringe)
glossary.bös: böse — angry (short form; bös werden: to grow angry); also bad, wicked
glossary.erbarmte: sich erbarmen — took pity (3rd sg. past, reflexive)
glossary.ergehen: ergehen — to fare, to go with someone (impersonal, with the dative: wie ergeht es ihm, how does it go with him)
glossary.erhalten: sich erhalten — to keep, maintain oneself (infinitive; sich auf den Füßen erhalten: to keep on one’s feet)
glossary.erzählt: erzählen — tells, relates (3rd sg. present; also the past participle)
glossary.gericht: das Gericht — dish, course of food (also: court of law)
glossary.haupt: das Haupt — head (elevated); also a head of lettuce or cabbage
glossary.hob: heben — lifted (3rd sg. past; hob … auf, from aufheben: picked up)
glossary.häupter: das Haupt — heads (pl.); here heads of lettuce
glossary.kehrte: zurückkehren — turned back, returned (3rd sg. past; particle zurück at the end)
glossary.kraut: das Kraut — cabbage, leafy greens (also: herb, plant)
glossary.leide: leiden — suffer (1st sg. present; Hunger leiden: to go hungry)
glossary.meinigen: das Meinige — what is mine, my own (substantivized possessive, dat.)
glossary.sage: sagen — say, tell (1st sg. present; wie ich euch sage: as I tell you)
glossary.schatz: der Schatz — treasure; also the everyday word for a sweetheart, darling
glossary.stürzen: stürzen — to plunge, fall headlong (herab stürzen: to plunge down)
glossary.todten: todt — dead (adj., inflected; 1857 spelling of tot)
glossary.trank: der Trank — draught, potion (also trank, drank, 3rd sg. past of trinken)
glossary.verlangt: verlangen — ask for, demand (2nd pl. present; also the past participle)
glossary.weiß: wissen — to know (1st/3rd sg. present; not the adjective weiß, white)
glossary.zahl: zahlen — pay (1st sg. present; so zahl ich: then I pay)
glossary.zog: ziehen — went, travelled (3rd sg. past; zog weiter: went on his way)
